task.description: Independently re-gate design §11.9 (rework iteration 3) against ELIXIR-DEV's step-08 BLOCKER, re-deriving the fix's correctness from actual source rather than trusting CODE-DESIGNER's narrative, and scrutinizing OQ-13's residual-gap deferral against this project's evidence bar.
acceptance_criteria: Re-derive from test/support/tenant_template.ex's actual current code (not the design's paraphrase) that §11.9.2's fix (move Sandbox.mode(:auto) from ensure_template!/0's unconditional first line into the else branch) resolves ELIXIR-DEV's exact reproduction

Scrutinize OQ-13's 'async:true callers already build the template first' claim for whether it is a reliable guarantee or a reachable gap, and judge whether deferral is acceptable per core-directives.md's evidence bar
Verify §11.7's two new regression items are concrete and correctly scoped
Verify no implementation code is present in §11.9

result.summary:
PASS. All four checks independently re-derived from source, not inherited from CODE-DESIGNER's step-09 narrative.

1. FIX CORRECTNESS, RE-DERIVED FROM ACTUAL CODE: Read test/support/tenant_template.ex lines 67-129 directly. Confirmed exactly as the design states: line 82 (`Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`) is `ensure_template!/0`'s literal first statement, executed unconditionally BEFORE the `if template_ready?() do :ok else ... end` conditional at line 84 -- so on every :clone-path call, including the steady-state (template already built) case, this line fires and (per DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's real, non-no-op mode-change check-in with an empty exclusion list, already established at design §9.1) discards every connection the pool holds, including the calling test process's own in-flight, uncommitted Tenant-insert connection under provision_via_shared_connection/1's {shared, self()} or :auto mode. This is Mechanism 4 exactly, reintroduced via a call site (ensure_template!/0, invoked from provision_schema!/2's :clone clause) that §11.2/§11.4's original 'zero Sandbox.mode/2 calls' claim never audited. §11.9.2's fix -- moving that one statement to become the first statement inside the existing `else` branch (i.e., only firing when template_ready?() is false, immediately before the advisory-lock acquisition at line 97) -- is a straightforward, minimal, correctly-targeted structural reorder: on the steady-state path (template_ready?() == true, which is every call after a partition's first, per the unchanged @built_marker_key persistent_term idempotency at §4.2), the function now returns :ok with zero Sandbox.mode/2 calls anywhere in its body, which directly closes the exact reproduction path ELIXIR-DEV found (backfill_test.exs 4/5 -> 0/5, all failures Ecto.InvalidChangesetError/tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey does not exist, caused by this same call discarding the caller's own Tenant insert before clone_tenant_schema!/1's Registration insert ran). The fix touches only this one line's position; template_ready?/0, clone_tenant_schema!/1, build_template!/0, and every other function in the file are correctly left untouched, matching §11.9.4's own implementation scope. §11.2 and §11.4 are corrected IN PLACE (not merely appended to) -- both sections' original unqualified 'zero Sandbox.mode/2 calls of any kind, anywhere in this function's call tree' claims are struck and replaced with the qualified, now-true version ('zero calls once template_ready?/0 is true'), each edit marked '(CORRECTED, REWORK ITERATION 3)' with the false original text quoted and the reasoning for the correction stated -- satisfying the acceptance criterion that these be corrected, not silently patched around.

2. OQ-13 SCRUTINIZED HARD, INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST: Ran my own greps rather than trusting the design's population count. Confirmed independently: of the 47 real `provisioned_tenant!(` call sites, exactly two are genuine async:true + TenantFixture callers using the default template: :clone -- test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs (verified by reading both files' provisioned_tenant/1 helper: neither passes a template: override, so both hit the default :clone path). The third async:true file grepped, test/letflow/iss0480_provisioning_repo_isolation_test.exs, has zero TenantFixture involvement by its own inline comment -- correctly excluded by the design's own count. This confirms the design's 'at least one async:true TenantFixture caller exists today' premise is factually correct, re-derived from source rather than inherited.

However, the reliability question is real and the design does not overclaim it. Read scripts/test_parallel.sh in full: MIX_TEST_PARTITION-based partitioning uses Mix's own `--partitions N` file-hash distribution across N independently-launched `mix test` OS processes, each its own BEAM VM/database. ExUnit's 'sync modules run after all async modules complete' ordering is real and holds WITHIN each partition, but WHICH files land in which partition is hash-derived, not designed -- so a partition that receives an async:false+:clone caller but neither secrets_test.exs nor webhooks_test.exs in its own async phase is a structurally reachable configuration, not merely a hypothetical one. The design's §11.9.3 does not claim otherwise -- it explicitly states this is 'currently unobserved... not asserted as proven,' names the exact mechanism that could break it, and provides three named, individually-reasoned rejected alternatives (retargeting the build's :auto call through ProvisioningRepo -- rejected because it would split the throwaway row's own insert and DDL across connections, reproducing a previously-diagnosed different failure the module's own existing comment already documents; eager pre-build from test_helper.exs -- rejected as a materially larger, out-of-scope mechanism, correctly deferred rather than absorbed under schedule pressure; reordering provision_via_shared_connection/1 to build-before-insert -- rejected as inverting §11.2's own deliberate parity-with-with_provisioning_repo/1 sequencing, correctly identified as the anti-patterns.md-warned shape of fixing a defect by rearranging an unrelated caller).

Judged against core-directives.md's actual evidence bar (Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source; Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching, which requires a demonstrated, MEASURED mechanism for any attribution, never an assertion that one probably holds): OQ-13's deferral is acceptable, not a blocking gap, for three concrete reasons distinct from CODE-DESIGNER's own framing (independently reasoned here, not merely re-stated): (a) the design does not ask anyone to trust the empirical expectation -- §11.7 item 6 makes the full-suite run a REQUIRED, named check (exact command, exact quoted Result: line, explicit 4/5->5/5 threshold) and §11.8 OQ-12 already states 'do not merge until that full-suite run is PASS' as an existing, independent hard gate -- so this is not a gap left to silently ride along until someone notices; (b) if the gap DOES fire during that required run, OQ-13's own text commits to treating it as a real, attributable, must-escalate finding (same named symptom, same named mechanism) rather than something a future run could wave through as 'known/expected noise' -- which is exactly what Failure Attribution's anti-count-matching rule demands; (c) the affected population is honestly bounded (at most one call outcome per partition, only in the from-scratch/first-call case, only if the async phase's own file-hash draw excludes both current async:true TenantFixture callers) and the failure mode if it does occur is the SAME already-diagnosed symptom, not a new, harder-to-triage failure class -- so a future occurrence is self-diagnosing via this section, not a silent trap. This is a genuine known-limitation-with-a-verification-gate, not an ambiguity or a deferred design decision left for ELIXIR-DEV to guess at during implementation -- nothing about implementing §11.9.4 requires resolving OQ-13 first.

3. §11.7 NEW ITEMS 5-6 CONCRETE AND CORRECTLY SCOPED: Item 5 (tenant_template_test.exs must stay green, unmodified) is scoped correctly -- confirmed via the design's own grep claim (zero Sandbox.mode references in that file) that this is a narrow, low-risk re-run, not requiring new test content, and correctly flags an unexpected failure there as a new finding requiring escalation rather than something to patch around. Item 6 (backfill_test.exs exact command, quoted Result: line, explicit 4/5-minimum-post-fix / 5/5-target threshold, mandated to be read from the specific file's own result rather than a broader suite summary) is exactly the fail-then-pass discipline this whole rework was found by, correctly restated as a permanent named regression check rather than folded anonymously into 'the suite passes.' Both are actionable by TEST-RUNNER/ELIXIR-DEV without further interpretation.

4. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE: Read §11.9 in full (11.9.1-11.9.5). The one code-shaped fragment present (`Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`, quoted in §11.9.1 and referenced in §11.9.2/§11.9.4) is a verbatim citation of the EXISTING line being relocated, used for traceability to source -- the same citation style already used elsewhere in this design (§9.7's own verbatim quote of the same line). §11.9.4's implementation instructions to ELIXIR-DEV are stated entirely as structural/positional description (which existing statement moves, to which existing branch, relative to which existing lines) with explicit call-outs of what must NOT change (template_ready?/0, clone_tenant_schema!/1, build_template!/0, do_build_template!/1, tenant_fixture.ex, data_case.ex) -- no new function bodies, no new branches' contents, no new Elixir logic authored in the design document itself. Passes.

VERDICT: PASS. §11.9 (and its in-place corrections to §11.2/§11.4/§11.7) is approved as the normative design for this rework. Route to ELIXIR-DEV to apply the single-statement reorder to test/support/tenant_template.ex's ensure_template!/0 per §11.9.4, then re-run §11.7's full regression plan (items 1-6, with particular attention to items 5 and 6's exact quoted command output) before proceeding to SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER and the §11.8 OQ-12 full-suite gate.
result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV to implement §11.9.4's single-statement reorder in test/support/tenant_template.ex's ensure_template!/0 (existing branch work in data_case.ex/tenant_fixture.ex from step-08 stays valid, do not redo), then re-run §11.7's full regression plan including its two new items (tenant_template_test.exs green, backfill_test.exs exact command/result-line re-verification), then proceed toward SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER and complete the §11.8 OQ-12 full-suite scripts/test_parallel.sh run before merge (do not merge until that run is PASS, per the design's own existing gate).
